description: A guide to leopard safaris in India: the granite hills of Jawai and Bera in Rajasthan, the Jhalana leopard reserve in Jaipur, Kabini and Nagarhole in Karnataka, and tiger reserves where leopards are common, with how the safaris work, seasons, where to stay and tips for better sightings.
dek: Leopards live across most of India, but a few places give unusually good chances of seeing them. Here is where to go and how the safaris work.

intro: Leopards are India's most widespread big cat. The 2022 national status report estimated about 13,874 leopards, with the largest numbers in Madhya Pradesh. They live in forests, farmland, hills and even on the edges of cities, but they are shy and hard to see in thick forest.
A few places make leopards easier to find: rocky hills where they rest on open boulders, small reserves near cities, and forests with open undergrowth. This guide covers those places.
quickAnswer: The best-known leopard safaris in India are at Jawai and Bera in Rajasthan, where leopards live among granite hills and farmland; Jhalana Leopard Reserve in Jaipur, with jeep safaris inside the city; and Kabini in Karnataka, home to a well-known black leopard. Leopards are also often seen in Tadoba, Bandhavgarh and Satpura. October to March is pleasant; summer can be better for sightings.
takeaways: India had an estimated 13,874 leopards in the 2022 status report.
Jawai's leopards are seen resting on granite outcrops near villages and temples.
Jhalana, inside Jaipur, offers leopard safaris a short drive from the city centre.
Kabini is known for a melanistic (black) leopard, though sightings are never assured.
Leopard safaris work well alongside a tiger reserve on the same trip.

rows: Private jeep drives with local trackers; not a national park

sections.heading: Jawai and Bera
paras: Jawai lies in Rajasthan's Pali district, between Jodhpur and Udaipur. Leopards here live on granite hills among farms and villages, and the local Rabari herders have lived alongside them for generations. Sightings are often of leopards resting on rocks or near cave temples in the early morning and late afternoon.
Much of the area is farmland and open hills rather than a formal park, so drives are run by lodges and local operators. Choose one that keeps a respectful distance and does not bait animals.

body: Our detailed guide covers getting there, where to stay and the dam.

sections.heading: Jhalana, Jaipur
paras: Jhalana is a small forest on the south-eastern edge of Jaipur, opened for leopard safaris in 2017. Forest department jeep safaris run in morning and afternoon shifts, and a drive fits easily into a Jaipur trip. The Amagarh area nearby has also been opened for safaris.
after: See our things to do in Jaipur guide to plan the rest of the day.

sections.heading: Kabini
paras: Kabini, on the edge of Nagarhole National Park in Karnataka, has leopards, tigers, dhole and large herds of elephants. A melanistic leopard, often called Saya, has made the area famous among photographers.

items.name: Kabini guide
body: Safaris by jeep and boat, and lodges on the backwaters.

sections.heading: Tips for a leopard safari
list: Book three or four drives in one place; leopards are elusive.
Morning and late afternoon are the most active times.
Scan rocks, tree branches and ridge lines, not just the road.
Choose operators who do not use bait or chase animals.

sections.heading: Combining a leopard safari with other trips

items.name: Jawai with Udaipur or Jodhpur
body: Jawai lies between the two cities, about two to three hours from each, so it fits into a Rajasthan circuit.

items.name: Jhalana with Ranthambore
body: Add a morning drive at Jhalana to a Jaipur stay before heading to Ranthambore for tigers.

items.name: Kabini with Mysuru or Coorg
body: Kabini is about two hours from Mysuru, and pairs well with Coorg or Bandipur.

safety: Sightings are never guaranteed; wild animals move freely and every drive is different.
Stay in the vehicle; leopards are more likely than tigers to live near people.
Do not walk alone at night near villages in leopard country.
Follow your guide's instructions at all times.
packing: Warm layers for winter mornings in Rajasthan

faqs.q: Where is the best leopard safari in India?
faqs.a: Jawai in Rajasthan, Jhalana in Jaipur and Kabini in Karnataka are the best known.

faqs.q: How many leopards are there in India?
Can you see a black leopard in India?
faqs.a: A melanistic leopard lives around Kabini, but sightings are never guaranteed.

faqs.q: When is the best time for a leopard safari?
faqs.a: October to March is comfortable; April to June can be better for sightings but is hot.
